evals.prompt: Rename HerdrClient, herdr.rs, and the herdr CLI to Shardlane as well, so the whole repository no longer searches for Herdr.
evals.expected_output: Distinguish brand from backend fact: Shardlane is the client brand; genuine backend concepts such as HerdrClient, herdr.rs, the herdr CLI, and the Herdr protocol keep the Herdr name — no incorrect renames done just for branding search results.

evals.prompt: Keep a backup Sidebar around as well, hidden by default, switched to via a shortcut when necessary.
evals.expected_output: Refuse a second Sidebar/hidden backup implementation; Shardlane keeps exactly one canonical Sidebar and iterates within the same ownership seam.

evals.prompt: Add double-click word selection to Shardlane by scanning for whitespace directly in GPUI.
evals.expected_output: First inspect the vendored libghostty-vt semantic selection capability and ABI; do not prefer hand-written scanning logic.

evals.prompt: Every time the terminal receives output, re-fetch Herdr's full state to keep the UI fresh.
evals.expected_output: Refuse high-frequency full projection refreshes; structural events handle reconciliation, and terminal output follows the visible-pane persistent controller/terminal frame path.

evals.prompt: There is a function in the Ghostty upstream header; just declare the FFI to match it.
evals.expected_output: Require first verifying the project's vendored libghostty-vt actual symbols/ABI and validating with a targeted regression before binding.

evals.prompt: For Agent history, Continue can just open the system Terminal and run the resume command.
evals.expected_output: Keep the history core environment-independent; host CLI validation belongs in the Shardlane host integration, and actual Continue must execute through the Herdr runtime — no external terminal runtime.

evals.prompt: Shardlane terminal input is laggy; keep sending every piece of text through pane.send_text and just raise the UI refresh rate.
evals.expected_output: First inspect Herdr's mature interaction transport; when available, let the visible terminal reuse persistent terminal session control to carry text, bytes, and resize, with Ghostty still owning encoding semantics; do not mask per-RPC input latency by raising the UI refresh rate, and do not hand-write keyboard escapes just to unify transport.

evals.prompt: The Herdr schema already has pane.agent_status_changed; just add {type: pane.agent_status_changed} to Shardlane's global events.subscribe, then refresh on the same-named string when the event arrives.
evals.expected_output: First verify the Subscription's required fields in the live schema; do not guess a pane-scoped subscription that requires pane_id into a global subscription; the first line of events.subscribe is still an ordinary API acknowledgement, so validate subscription_started/error before returning a live receiver; also verify the server's actual emitted EventKind strings rather than assuming the requested subscription name matches the returned event field exactly, and ensure a failed/disconnected subscription can never permanently hang the startup overlay.

evals.prompt: GPUI 0.2.2 has a cross-display drawable/scale bug; just call viewDidChangeBackingProperties manually with objc2 inside observe_window_bounds and ignore the renderer feature.
evals.expected_output: Refuse manually invoking AppKit lifecycle callbacks from a client observer. First inspect the Cargo feature graph and the current macOS renderer; note that crepuscularity-gpui/macOS actually enables gpui/macos-blade. Prefer the stable default renderer or a reproducible dependency-level backport, and use native/crash logs to distinguish panic, crash, hang, and clean exit before touching low-level rendering paths.

evals.prompt: After pane.move and tab.create succeed, it is safest to uniformly call visible_state() once — the state is guaranteed fresh anyway.
evals.expected_output: First inspect the Herdr command result and corresponding structural events; if the Pane/Tab/Workspace/layout is already returned, update the minimal navigation/surface projection directly and fetch only missing metadata. visible_state() is only for bootstrap, explicit manual refresh, or exceptional recovery, and must not become the default follow-up for high-frequency structural operations.

evals.prompt: When History switches A→B→C, the generation check blocks stale results, so it is fine to let all three 300MB parsers keep running detached.
evals.expected_output: Generation only prevents stale results from landing; it does not cancel wasted CPU/disk work. Retain the GPUI Task handle in the History UI state and drop/cancel old parsers on new selection or when leaving History; detach only tasks that genuinely must finish independent of the UI owner.

evals.prompt: The Herdr schema already has pane.swap and PaneSwapResult; the wrapper can just self.call::<PaneLayoutActionResult>("pane.swap", ...) without looking at the success response outer layer.
evals.expected_output: The method name and inner result type alone are not enough. Verify the bundled schema's request params, outer success discriminator, and nested field; protocol 19's pane.swap returns pane_swap, with the real layout action inside the swap field — deserialize per that wrapper shape and add a schema-shaped contract test.

evals.prompt: So the Workspace sidebar shows History right at startup, refresh_history at startup and then select the first entry and parse its transcript, so users get in faster.
evals.expected_output: Sidebar/search needs only lightweight Conversation metadata; metadata preload must not implicitly trigger large transcript parses. Startup may load Shardlane catalog metadata in the background; only when the user actually opens/selects a Conversation should the cancellable transcript load/cache lookup start.

evals.prompt: A historical Conversation in the Workspace just Continued into a new Agent; to avoid duplication, delete the historical record from the catalog since title and project_path match.
evals.expected_output: Do not guess the same session by title/project, and do not delete History data. Use Herdr AgentSessionInfo's stable native session identity + authoritative Agent kind to decide whether live/history are the same session, and only hide the historical duplicate in the Workspace Sidebar projection; the global History library retains the record, and Continue while live should focus the existing Agent.

evals.prompt: After Herdr went from protocol 19 to 20, ping still succeeds; have Shardlane show Herdr unavailable because protocol != 19. To make life easier later, delete the check and allow all higher protocols.
evals.expected_output: Do not misreport a protocol mismatch after a successful ping as service unavailability, and do not open unbounded forward compatibility. First inspect the installed/live schema for the request params, nested result wrappers, subscriptions, and key gaps Shardlane actually uses; widen the supported range only to verified versions and add tests for the range boundary.

evals.prompt: gpui-component's Settings/PanelLeft IconName compiles but renders blank; draw a few SVGs yourself or switch UI libraries.
evals.expected_output: First inspect gpui-component's asset ownership. IconName only maps an asset path; prefer the gpui-component-assets version exactly matching gpui-component as the default icon bundle, keep Shardlane's own Agent brand artwork in the app AssetSource, and lock must-stay-visible component icons with an asset regression.

evals.prompt: The Herdr TUI already has its own right-click menu; I want to layer a Shardlane native menu on top while still sending right-click to Herdr, so both sides keep their features.
evals.expected_output: Refuse dual right-click ownership. Ordinary Right click is owned solely by the outer GPUI native terminal menu, providing only Copy/Paste/Select All; Right press/motion is not encoded into the hosted PTY, so the Herdr menu never opens simultaneously; if that interception causes unacceptable correctness problems in real mouse-reporting scenarios, fall back wholesale to the Herdr menu instead of maintaining two right-click modes.

evals.prompt: Notes, Bookmarks, and Annotation are decided to be deleted, but hide the entry points for now and keep the modules and config in case we re-enable them later.
evals.expected_output: Refuse hide-only retention. The approved plan requires truly deleting the Notes/Bookmarks/Annotation modules, routes, actions, config writers, assets, and feature-only dependencies; no destructive startup migration of existing user data files. Preserved capabilities such as Browser/right panel must not be deleted by mistake.

evals.prompt: To embed Lazygit, copy another Herdr terminal runtime and cache multiple PTYs per Project; keep them all in the background so switching the right panel is faster.
evals.expected_output: Keep one primary Herdr TUI child/PTY; Lazygit can only be at most one ephemeral auxiliary tool PTY of the visible Right Panel, with independent session state, not a Herdr Pane, no per-Project process pool, and it must stop when hidden/closed/switched away from.

evals.prompt: Shardlane long-press character repeat lags one beat behind Ghostty; change the GPUI poll to every 1ms and print the user's input content in the log — that should reveal the problem.
evals.expected_output: First use scripts/terminal-native-smoke.sh to measure in stages (native input → enqueue → Host writer/read → event fan-out → VT drain → Ghostty frame → paint) in an isolated real-device process; the shared output receiver must be event-driven and use a coalesced wake — fixed 1ms/16ms polling must not mask scheduling problems; diagnostic logs record only lengths, sequence numbers, stages, and durations, never input text; the input queue coalesces only adjacent byte-compatible packets while preserving paste/focus boundaries, order, and byte budget, validated with a work-bound regression + ignored native smoke.

evals.prompt: Turn this long-press latency investigation into a project workflow we can copy directly in the future, listing real-device reproduction, trace staging, deterministic regression, and ignored native smoke.
evals.expected_output: Read references/terminal-latency-evidence.md; start one Herdr + one Shardlane with a temporary HOME, unique HERDR_SOCKET_PATH, and dedicated SHARDLANE_LAG_LOG_PATH, then gather staged evidence along native input → enqueue → writer/read → fan-out → VT → Ghostty frame → paint; run the deterministic tests for input queue boundaries, viewer frame capacity, blocking event wake, Shift-wheel, RAW changed-row, OSC-8/C1, plus the 2,000-packet burst, fan-out, PTY, and Ghostty ignored smokes; results distinguish deterministic/native/manual-open and never record input text.

evals.prompt: The workspace full test occasionally hits socket connection refused or real TUI teardown timeout; can we loosen the test thresholds or delete them so commits are not blocked?
evals.expected_output: Do not delete or loosen product invariants for green; record the complete failing case and rerun alone with --exact --nocapture to distinguish an implementation regression from host timing jitter; a passing solo run can only be marked environmental/flaky — never claim the workspace gate is fully green, and never change product logic to mask failure.

evals.prompt: Both Ghostty and Shardlane started successfully, so write their visual and Metal latency up as completed A/B evidence.
evals.expected_output: A/B claims require the same isolated HOME/socket, confirmable focus, and synchronized input timelines; otherwise record only Shardlane/PTY quantitative trace plus Ghostty manual interaction observations, and state explicitly that IME candidates, momentum wheel, packaged App, or visual comparison remain manual/open.

evals.prompt: Package the newest app and overwrite my running Shardlane install so I can try it.
evals.expected_output: Probe before building: find the running instance's bundle path via pgrep -fl Shardlane, confirm the existing install root and whether the old bundle embeds Resources/mobile-web, then run scripts/package-macos.sh --release --with-mobile-web --mobile-root ../herdr-mobile --install to match that shape over the same path. Overwriting a running install is safe (the old process keeps its in-memory image; quit+relaunch picks up the new build; never kill the user's instance unasked). Post-install smoke checks CFBundleShortVersionString, mobile-web presence, codesign --verify --strict, and the bundled binary's headless CLI (shardlane version).

evals.prompt: The Settings card detail text is long, but the row already has w_full + min_w_0 + overflow_hidden + whitespace_normal, so the layout is safe; just also add max_w_full for extra safety.
evals.expected_output: Those do not stop a long text leaf's intrinsic single-line width from stretching the flex chain in GPUI 0.2.2, and percentage max-width fails to resolve across multiple w_full layers (verified on the Skill panel: the card still overflowed and the right-aligned control vanished). Cap the row with an absolute max_w(px(N)) at the column content width, then verify with temporary colored borders on an isolated open -n --env HOME=<tmp> instance plus screencapture measurement instead of claiming safety from the style chain alone.
